mainTopic: Whether forced giving counts as 'giving' under הלל's תקנה, the rule that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and why a גט given on condition that the paper be returned is valid.
overview: The amud begins by asking whether giving money to someone against his will counts as 'giving.' This matters for a גט given 'on condition that you give me two hundred זוז.' רבא tries to learn the answer from הלל's תקנה about a house in a walled city, and the גמרא reports two opposite versions of his proof. רב פפא (or רב שימי בר אשי) rejects both, so הלל's תקנה proves nothing either way. Next, רבי יוחנן rules that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the משנה except in three cases: ערב, צידן and ראיה אחרונה. Then a ברייתא says a husband who keeps the paper of the גט for himself has not divorced his wife, but if he makes returning the paper a condition, she is divorced. רב חסדא explains this through רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and אביי through רבי מאיר's doubled condition. רבא gives his own reason: the action came before the condition. רב אדא בר אהבה then challenges רבא from בני גד ובני ראובן, where the condition and the action were about two separate matters, and his argument continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא's inference: forced giving normally doesn't count
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes his proof from הלל's תקנה: since הלל needed a special rule, giving against someone's will normally does not count as נתינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can learn from this that, in general, giving something to a person against his will is not considered giving.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is finishing his proof. Because הלל had to make a special תקנה so that money could be given to an unwilling buyer, regular giving against someone's will must not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is: if forced giving already worked, הלל would not have needed his תקנה. So the תקנה shows that without it, forced giving is not valid. Carried over to a conditional גט, if the wife forces the 200 זוז on her husband, the condition is not fulfilled.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference; we can learn by implication

steps.whyThisMatters: This decides whether a wife can fulfill a 'give me money' condition on her גט by forcing the money on her husband.

phrases.english: By inference, that in general,
phrases.notes: In general means outside the special case where הלל made his תקנה.

phrases.english: giving against his will
is not considered giving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's statement about הלל's תקנה, which began just before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That giving against the receiver's will is normally not valid giving.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The תקנה of הלל allowing the seller of a house in a walled city to give the money even when the buyer would not accept it.

steps.title: רב פפא: maybe Hillel's rule was only for when the buyer was absent
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא (or רב שימי בר אשי) rejects the proof. Maybe הלל's תקנה was needed only when the buyer was not there. In his presence, even forced giving might count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא, and some say רב שימי בר אשי, objected: Maybe הלל needed his תקנה only for giving when the buyer was not present. But in his presence, giving counts whether he agrees or not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's proof. It suggests that הלל's תקנה covered a different situation: the buyer was not present.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed הלל's rule was about the receiver being unwilling. רב פפא says it may have been about the receiver being absent. If so, nothing is proven about forced giving face to face, and in the case of the גט the wife gives the money to her husband in person.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (a different name for who said it)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa objected to it,
and some say it was Rav Shimi bar Ashi:
But perhaps when he needed to institute it,
phrases.notes: 'He' is הלל, and 'it' is his rule letting the seller give the money to an unwilling buyer.

phrases.english: it was for when it was not in his presence,
but in his presence,
whether with his consent or against his will,
it is considered giving!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's inference by giving הלל's תקנה a different reason.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from הלל's תקנה only; no opposite ruling is proven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The תקנה might have been needed because the buyer was absent, not because he was unwilling, so it says nothing about forced giving in person.

steps.title: Second version: רבא infers that forced giving in person does count
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רבא learns the opposite from הלל's תקנה. הלל's rule was needed only when the buyer was absent, so giving in person counts even against the receiver's will. A wife who forces the 200 זוז on her husband has fulfilled the condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say a different version. רבא said: From הלל's תקנה we learn that if a husband says, 'Here is your גט on condition that you give me two hundred זוז,' and she gave it to him, it counts as giving whether he agreed or not. הלל needed his תקנה only when the giving was not in the person's presence. But in his presence, it counts whether he agrees or not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רבא's statement. In this version רבא himself uses the 'not in his presence' reading, and so concludes that giving face to face counts even if forced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reading that רב פפא suggested in step 2 is now the basis of רבא's own proof. Since הלל's תקנה was only for the absent buyer, giving in person must already have worked without it, even against the receiver's will. That is applied directly to the conditional גט.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (a second version follows)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument from רבא. It is a second report of what רבא said, and it reaches the opposite result from step 1.

phrases.english: And some say: Rava said:
From the ordinance of Hillel we learn:
If he said: 'This is your bill of divorce'

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּתְּנִי לִי מָאתַיִם זוּז״,
phrases.english: 'on condition that you give me two hundred zuz,'
and she gave it to him,
whether with his consent or against his will,
it is considered giving;
and when Hillel needed to institute his ordinance,
it was for when it was not in his presence,
but in his presence,
whether with his consent or against his will,
it is considered giving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of רבא's statement. It uses the reading from step 2 and reaches the opposite conclusion from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If she gives the 200 זוז to her husband in person, it counts as giving even if he does not want to accept it.

steps.title: רב פפא: maybe even in person, forced giving doesn't count
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא (or רב שימי בר אשי) rejects the second version too. Maybe even in person, only giving with consent counts. הלל made his rule for the absent case simply because that was the problem he needed to fix.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא, and some say רב שימי בר אשי, objected: Maybe even in his presence, giving with his consent counts, but against his will it does not. הלל simply fixed the problem that needed fixing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the second version of רבא's proof. It shows that הלל's תקנה does not prove that forced giving in person works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's second proof assumed that if הלל only fixed the absent case, the in-person case must already work. רב פפא answers that הלל addressed only the real-life problem: the buyer was hiding. That says nothing about whether forced giving in person is valid, so the question about the גט is left open.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions of רבא try to learn from הלל's תקנה whether forced giving counts, and both are rejected. The תקנה can be explained either way, so it proves nothing about the conditional גט.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa objected to it,
and some say it was Rav Shimi bar Ashi:
But perhaps even in his presence as well,
with his consent, yes, it counts;
against his will, no, it does not;
and Hillel instituted what he needed to.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the second version of רבא's inference.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from הלל's תקנה in the second version; the question itself stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: הלל's rule being limited to the absent case does not show that forced giving in person works. הלל may have simply addressed the problem that actually came up.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל except in three cases
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל wherever he is quoted in the משנה, except in three places: ערב, צידן and ראיה אחרונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: wherever רבן שמעון בן גמליאל taught something in our משנה, the הלכה follows him. There are three exceptions: the guarantor case, the צידן case, and the case of evidence brought at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a general rule about how to decide הלכה whenever רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives an opinion in the משנה, along with three exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a single תנא's opinion does not beat the חכמים. רבי יוחנן says רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is special, so the הלכה follows him even when he stands alone. One of the three exceptions, צידן, ties to the case in our perek about giving a גט on condition of getting back a coat.

keyTerms.meaning: The final law follows his opinion
A guarantor who backs up a loan (בבא בתרא)
A city. Here it means the case in our perek connected to an event there
The last dispute about evidence brought late to court (סנהדרין)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule for deciding הלכה across all of ש״ס, not only in גיטין. It also tells us that in the צידן case the הלכה does not follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Every place where he taught
(that is, Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel) in our Mishnah
the halacha follows him;
except for the guarantor, and Tzaidan,
phrases.notes: These are short nicknames for cases. 'Guarantor' is in בבא בתרא, and 'צידן' is the case connected to our perek.

phrases.english: and the final evidence.
phrases.notes: That's the last dispute about evidence brought late to court, in סנהדרין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section. It is a general ruling tied to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's opinion in our משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the משנה except in the cases of ערב, צידן and ראיה אחרונה.

steps.title: The paper is mine compared with return the paper to me
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: if the husband says the paper stays his, she is not divorced. If he makes it a condition that she return the paper, she is divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: if he says 'Here is your גט, but the paper is mine,' she is not divorced. If he says 'on condition that you give me back the paper,' she is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with two cases about who owns the paper of the גט. It sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case the husband keeps the paper for himself, so he has not really given her a גט. In the second case the גט is fully hers, and returning the paper is just a condition she will fulfill later.

keyTerms.meaning: The paper the גט is written on
On condition that you give back

steps.confusionAlert: In both cases the paper ends up back with the husband. The difference is whether he kept ownership from the start or truly gave it and only attached a condition.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"Here is your bill of divorce,
but the paper is mine" –
she is not divorced.
"On condition that you return the paper to me" –
she is divorced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא that the גמרא will connect back to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Keeping the paper as his own makes the גט invalid. Requiring the paper to be returned as a condition still allows a valid divorce.

steps.title: Why do the two halves of the ברייתא differ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the two cases have different results, since either way the paper goes back to the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between the first case and the second case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the two rulings seem not to fit together and asks for the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second case she must give the paper back, so she never really keeps it. That looks just like the first case, where the paper is his. So why is she divorced in one and not the other?

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the source
The last part of the source

phrases.english: What is different in the first clause
and what is different in the last clause?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא in step 6 by pointing to an apparent inconsistency.
steps.kashyaTarget: The different rulings in the two halves of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In both cases the husband ends up with the paper, so the rulings should be the same.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: she can pay the value
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the ברייתא follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who lets the wife pay the value instead of the item. So in the condition case the paper is truly hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: whose view is this? It is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who says she can give him its value. Here too, she can satisfy him with money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question by tying the ברייתא to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling about the coat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that when a גט depends on returning an item, she can pay its value instead. So in the condition case she does not have to give back this very paper, which means it truly belongs to her and the גט works. When the husband says 'the paper is mine,' it never became hers at all.
steps.whatToRemember: A גט given on condition that the paper be returned is valid because, according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, she may pay the paper's value. So the paper itself is fully hers.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Whose view is this? –
it is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
who said: she may give him its value;
phrases.notes: This is his ruling in our משנה about the husband's coat that got lost.

phrases.english: here too –
it is possible for her to satisfy him with money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא הָא מַנִּי רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הִיא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to a specific תנא whose view explains the difference
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the paper must be returned in both cases, the two cases should have the same result.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, she may return the value instead of the paper. So the paper is truly hers and the גט works. Keeping ownership of the paper outright does not work.

steps.title: אביי objects: paying the value may only work when the item is gone
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב חסדא. Perhaps רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only allows paying the value when the original item no longer exists. Here the paper still exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objects: Fine, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said you can pay the value when the item is no longer around. But where the item is still around, did he say that?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב חסדא's answer from step 8. He says רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule may not apply to our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא needed רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule (pay the value instead of the item) to explain why the paper truly belongs to the wife. אביי points out that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל may only allow this when the item is lost or gone. In our case the paper is right there, so the wife would have to return the actual paper, and רב חסדא's explanation falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it; a strong challenge to the previous statement
Say / Grant that; it admits one point in order to limit it
It is no longer in its original form; the item is gone or lost
It still exists in its original form

phrases.english: Abaye objects to this:

phrases.aramaic: אֵימוֹר דְּאָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל –
phrases.english: Say that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said this
phrases.notes: He means the rule from step 8: you may give the value instead of the item itself.

phrases.english: where the item no longer exists as it was;
where it still exists, did he say it?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's answer in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the ברייתא follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule of paying the value may only apply when the item is gone. Here the paper still exists, so his rule cannot explain the ברייתא.

steps.title: אביי's new answer: the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר's doubled-condition rule
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who requires a doubled condition. The husband here did not double his condition, so the condition does not hold him back and the גט works.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: Whose view is this ברייתא? It is רבי מאיר, who says a condition must be doubled. And here the husband did not double his condition.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי drops רב חסדא's explanation and gives his own reason why the wife is divorced in the 'condition' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, a condition only counts if both sides are spelled out: 'if you do it, this happens; if you don't, it doesn't.' The husband only said 'on condition that you return the paper' and never said what happens if she doesn't. So his condition does not count, and the גט works without it.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who requires a doubled condition
A doubled condition: stating both what happens if it is fulfilled and what happens if it is not

steps.confusionAlert: Here the גט is valid because the condition is weak and does not count. It is not valid because the condition was met.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Meir,
who says: we require a doubled condition;
phrases.notes: Doubled means saying both sides: 'if you do it, it works; if you don't, it doesn't.'

phrases.english: and here, he did not double his condition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב חסדא's rejected answer with a new explanation
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to a specific תנא (רבי מאיר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'condition' case works because the wife can pay the value of the paper (רב חסדא)
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'condition' case works because a condition that is not doubled does not count, according to רבי מאיר

steps.title: רבא objects: would a doubled condition really block the גט here?
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out what אביי's answer implies: if the husband had doubled the condition, it would not be a valid גט. He then sets up a challenge from the source of all conditions, בני גד ובני ראובן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objects: The reason it works is that he did not double his condition, which means that if he had doubled it, it would not be a valid גט. But where do we learn all the rules of conditions from? From the condition of בני גד ובני ראובן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא draws out what follows from אביי's answer. Then he starts setting up his attack by naming the source we learn all conditions from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אביי is right, everything depends on doubling: a doubled condition would block the גט. רבא wants to show that there is a different problem with this condition, one that applies whether or not it is doubled. To do that, he goes back to the source of all the rules of conditions: משה's deal with בני גד ובני ראובן. The next step finishes his point.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is; points to an implied opposite case
Now consider / After all; opens a basic premise
The tribes whose deal with משה (במדבר 32) is the model for all conditions

phrases.english: Rava objects to this:
The reason it works is that he did not double his condition;

phrases.aramaic: הָא כַּפְלֵיהּ לִתְנָאֵיהּ – לָא הָוֵי גִּיטָּא;
phrases.english: so if he had doubled his condition, it would not be a valid גט;

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדֵי כֹּל תְּנָאֵי מֵהֵיכָא גָּמְרִינַן לְהוּ?
phrases.english: Now, from where do we learn all conditions?
From the condition of the children of Gad and the children of Reuben;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what follows from אביי's answer and begins to challenge it
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the deciding factor is whether the condition was doubled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי's answer implies a doubled condition would block the גט. But the source of all conditions shows another requirement that this case does not meet anyway, so doubling cannot be what decides it.

steps.title: A condition must come before the action, and here it came after
steps.stepSummary: Just as with בני גד ובני ראובן the condition came before the action, every condition must come before the action. That leaves out our case, where the husband gave the גט first and stated the condition afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as there the condition came before the action, so every condition must come before the action. That leaves out our case, where the action came before the condition!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his challenge. He shows from the בני גד ובני ראובן model that our condition is already flawed because of its order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה first stated the condition and only then the result ('if they cross... you shall give them ארץ הגלעד'). The husband here did the reverse: 'Here is your גט' (the action) and then 'on condition that you return the paper' (the condition). Since this condition is already out of the proper order, doubling it or not cannot be what makes the difference, and אביי's reason does not stand.

keyTerms.meaning: The condition comes before the action
The action comes before the condition
Just as there... so too; a comparison to a model case

steps.whatToRemember: All rules of conditions come from בני גד ובני ראובן. One of those rules is that the condition must be said before the action. In our ברייתא the husband said the action first, so רבא says אביי's 'not doubled' reason cannot be what explains the case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This brings in a basic rule of conditions, תנאי קודם למעשה. It shows that the order of the words in a condition is a legal requirement in its own right, separate from doubling.

phrases.english: Just as there, the condition comes before the action,
so too, every condition must come before the action;
which excludes the case here, where the action comes before the condition!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's challenge using the source he named in step 11
steps.raayaObject: That our condition is already flawed because the action came before the condition, so doubling cannot decide the case
steps.raayaSupportSource: The condition of בני גד ובני ראובן (במדבר 32), where the condition was stated before the action

steps.title: רבא's own answer: the action came before the condition
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the גט is valid because the husband gave it first and attached the condition only afterward, so the condition does not take hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: the reason the גט works is that the action (giving the גט) came before the condition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops אביי's explanation and gives his own reason why the woman in the ברייתא is divorced. The husband did the action first and said the condition second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the rule from Step 12: a condition only works when it comes before the action, as with בני גד ובני ראובן. In our ברייתא the husband said 'here is your גט' and only then 'on condition that you return the paper.' A condition tacked on after the action does not hold back the גט, so the divorce takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the earlier answer and offers a new one
The action; here, the actual giving of the גט
A condition attached to an action

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main point of the coming discussion: whether the order of condition and action is what makes a condition work.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
because the action precedes the condition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rule just shown in Step 12 (condition must precede action) to give רבא's own answer, replacing the answers of רב חסדא and אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason replacing the rejected answers: the order of action and condition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We needed רבן שמעון בן גמליאל or רבי מאיר's doubled condition to explain why the גט works.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גט works simply because the condition was stated after the action, so it does not hold.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה questions רבא's reason
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה points out what רבא's answer implies: if the condition had come first, the גט would be invalid. He then starts to bring in the model of בני גד ובני ראובן to challenge that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה objected. Your reason is that the action came before the condition. That means if the condition came before the action, it would not be a valid גט. Now, where do we learn all the laws of conditions from? From the condition of בני גד ובני ראובן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה draws out what follows from רבא's answer. He is setting up his attack by going back to the source of all conditions, בני גד ובני ראובן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If order is the only reason the גט works, then a husband who said the condition first would have a valid condition, and the גט would not be valid at all, because she would have to give back the paper. רב אדא בר אהבה is about to show that the source case teaches a second requirement. That requirement would make the condition fail here no matter what the order was.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it; a sharp challenge
But then...; points out what follows from the statement
Now, after all; opens a logical argument

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava objected to it:
The reason is that the action precedes the condition,
but if the condition precedes the action,
it would not be a valid גט;
now, all conditions,
from where do we learn them?
From the condition of the children of Gad and the children of Reuben,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer from Step 13 by drawing out what it implies.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the order of condition and action is what decides this case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's answer means a condition stated first would block this גט. But the source case may disqualify this condition for a different reason, which would make order beside the point.

steps.title: The model case: condition about one thing, action about another
steps.stepSummary: In the case of בני גד ובני ראובן, the condition was about one matter and the action about a different matter. Every condition must follow that pattern. That leaves out our case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as there the condition was about one thing and the action about another thing, so too every condition must be like that. This leaves out the case here...
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה shows a second feature of the source case: the condition and the action were about different things. The sentence continues past this point to explain why our case is left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With בני גד ובני ראובן, the condition was fighting alongside the rest of Israel, and the action was receiving their land. Those are two separate matters. Since all conditions are learned from that case, a condition must likewise involve a matter separate from the action. Our case looks different, so it would be left out regardless of the order.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as there...; compares to the source case

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this is the same point as Step 12. Step 12 was about the order (condition first). This step adds a different requirement: the condition and the action must be about separate things.

phrases.english: Just as there,
the condition is about one matter
and the action is about another matter,
so too, every condition;
this excludes the case here,
phrases.notes: The sentence isn't finished yet. It continues on the next amud, which explains exactly how our case is different.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה הָתָם תְּנַאי בְּדָבָר אֶחָד וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּדָבָר אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the setup from Step 14 by stating the feature of the source case that רב אדא בר אהבה will use against רבא.
steps.raayaObject: That a valid condition must be about a matter separate from the action, which would leave out our case.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The condition of בני גד ובני ראובן, the source from which all conditions are learned.
